name: Gries im Sellrain
kurzbeschreibung: Gries im Sellrain – a small, peaceful village in the Sellrain Valley, surrounded by classic Tyrolean mountain scenery and traditional farming.
beschreibung:
Overview

Gries im Sellrain is situated at roughly 1,200 metres altitude in the romantic Sellraintal in the Tyrolean district of Innsbruck-Land, approximately 25 kilometres southwest of the provincial capital Innsbruck. This tranquil alpine community of around 620 residents is nestled at the junction where the Zirmbach torrent coming from Kühtai meets the Melach stream from the high-altitude Lüsens Valley. Framed by majestic peaks of the Stubai Alps such as the 2,646-metre Rosskogel, the Freihut, and the glaciated 3,298-metre Lüsener Fernerkogel, the village preserves an authentic rural heritage. Recognized as an official Mountaineering Village (Bergsteigerdorf) by the Alpine Clubs, Gries im Sellrain champions gentle, sustainable tourism, pristine natural environments, expansive stone pine forests, and quiet outdoor pursuits far from massive commercial resort development.

History

Settlement in this alpine valley commenced during the High Middle Ages when Tyrolean nobles such as Count Meinhard II established dairy farmsteads known as Schwaighöfe. Early homesteads in the parish, such as Marendebach, were documented as early as 1254, while the valley name Selrain first appeared in 1271. The place name Gries derives from the Middle High German term for gravel and riverbanks, reflecting the alluvial junction of the two wild mountain torrents. The parish church of St. Martin was erected between 1733 and 1735 by Innsbruck builder Franz Renn as a Baroque hall church, enriched with delicate Rococo stucco and frescoes by Johann Michael Strickner, incorporated into Wilten Abbey in 1786. The municipal coat of arms granted in 1978 displays five silver peaks on a black field, representing the pyramidal silhouette of the Lüsener Fernerkogel. Since 2013, Gries has proudly belonged to the prestigious network of Mountaineering Villages.

Getting There

By car, travellers reach Gries im Sellrain via the Inntal Autobahn A12, exiting at Zirl-Ost/Kematen in Tirol. From Kematen, the provincial road L13 climbs steadily through the Sellraintal for about 25 minutes directly into Gries. In summer, the village can also be reached from the Ötztal via the Kühtai Saddle, though winter avalanche closures may occur. Rail passengers arrive at Innsbruck Central Station, an international rail hub. From the station square, regional VVT bus line 4166 runs hourly direct services through Kematen to Gries and onward to Kühtai, completely free of charge for holidaymakers carrying the regional guest card.

Tips

In winter, Gries im Sellrain, along with the adjacent Lüsens Valley and Praxmar, serves as a world-renowned haven for ski touring enthusiasts; classic summits such as the 2,876-metre Lampsenspitze with its permanent avalanche safety educational trail draw mountaineers from all over Europe. For downhill skiing, Austria's highest winter sports resort Kühtai, situated at 2,020 metres with 47 kilometres of snow-sure pistes, lies just a 15-minute drive up the valley, while beginners enjoy the Sonnenberg village draglift. Families love the nearly 5-kilometre natural toboggan run descending from the traditional Juifenalm hut at nearly 2,000 metres. During summer, gentle hikes through fragrant stone pine forests, the Sellrain High Trail, and the spectacular crimson bloom of the alpine roses delight nature lovers.
